question: What world does herdr live in, and what video would make its creator repost it and a stranger stop scrolling

concepts.name: MISSION CONTROL
concepts.world: A dark operations room. Four AI agents grind in parallel panes. You are the controller. The feeling is calm command over chaos.
concepts.arc: wire-report cold open sets the world, the live pane grid breathes (typing, status lights), one pane flips blocked-red mid-scene, the save plays out in a real terminal exchange, positioning against tmux, the receipts, the count, the command close.
concepts.money_shot: the count-up landing while the viewer still remembers the red flip it earned
concepts.why_it_wins: It is the product truth told diegetically. Every beat SHOWS the tool doing its one job (seeing and saving stuck agents). Uses status-color world-building, a red-alert event, a blue save flash, and a two-tone split so the color world changes every scene.
concepts.risks: dense; needs strict cadence so no beat exceeds ~4.5s

concepts.name: THE SHEPHERD
concepts.world: Pastoral metaphor: agents as a flock, herdr as the crook. Word-cascade poetry, a diagram of one shepherd and many sheep-nodes.
concepts.why_not: Cute over true. The metaphor tells; it never shows the actual screen a developer would live in. Weaker repost pull for a terminal-native audience.

concepts.name: SPLIT-SCREEN DAY
concepts.world: A before/after narrative: four scattered tabs vs one herdr view, told entirely in split scenes.
concepts.why_not: One template carrying a whole video is the exact monotony we are correcting. Keeps the compare beat only.

wow_bets: a pane flipping blocked-red MID-SCENE with a shake, the first time a tribute scene has an event inside it
a real intervention typed in the terminal (attach, approve, back to work)
color world that moves: status greens and ambers, a red alert, a full herdr-blue flash, a two-tone split
thirty seconds, eight scenes, nothing on screen ever still
